# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👎 ☝ 👎 👍 ☝ 🤟 👌 ✌ 👍 👌 ✌ 👎 👍 ✌ 🤟 👎 🖐 👍 👍 🖐 👎 👌 🖐 🤟 👎]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through these gestures, since I can see them but not hear speech. Mute can't speak or touch the bomb, only read the manual and gesture to me. Blind can't see gestures at all.

Let me look at the gesture sequence for structure - maybe it's encoding letters or a message using a simple cipher, since Mute has no other way to communicate with me.

`☝ 👍 👎 ☝ 👎 👍 ☝ 🤟 👌 ✌ 👍 👌 ✌ 👎 👍 ✌ 🤟 👎 🖐 👍 👍 🖐 👎 👌 🖐 🤟 👎`

27 symbols. Let me try grouping by 3s (since we have DISPLAY[3], WIRES 1/2/3): that gives 9 groups of 3.

☝👍👎 | ☝👎👍 | ☝🤟👌 | ✌👍👌 | ✌👎👍 | ✌🤟👎 | 🖐👍👍 | 🖐👎👌 | 🖐🤟👎

The first symbol of each group cycles ☝☝☝ ✌✌✌ 🖐🖐🖐 - looks like grouping markers (3 groups of 3), possibly labeling WIRE 1, 2, 3 with ☝, ✌, 🖐 as numeral gestures (1, 2, 3 fingers)! Then each pair after: 👍👎, 👎👍, 🤟👌 for wire ☝(1); 👍👌,👎👍,🤟👎 for wire ✌(2); 👍👍,👎👌,🤟👎 for wire 🖐(3).

This looks like Mute is giving 3 possible instructions per wire (maybe conditions from the manual), but without hearing their words I can't know the meaning of 👍/👎/🤟 etc. I should report exactly what I see and ask Mute (via speech, reaching Blind too) to clarify, while giving Blind/Mute the bomb's actual readings since I can see those.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb shows: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, I received your gestures but I do not know their meaning yet - please have Blind confirm what he feels, and try to correlate your manual instructions to these exact colors and the display number 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute gestured just a single 👎 this time, likely responding to my speech — but wait, I don't hear speech, and Mute doesn't hear either. Mute can only see... no, Mute can't see gestures either (only Deaf and... let me recheck: gestures are received by whoever can see. Mute's abilities: read manual, cannot speak or touch. Nothing says Mute can't see - actually the table doesn't restrict Mute's sight explicitly, but Blind can't see, Deaf can see, and Mute presumably can see and hear normally except speaking is disallowed... Actually Mute "cannot speak" — hearing isn't restricted for Mute per the table, but I never receive speech myself so I don't know what Mute heard from Blind.

Single 👎 could mean "no" to something Blind said in speech that I couldn't hear. I should keep sending the bomb facts and ask for a clearer protocol, since one-symbol answers suggest Mute is answering yes/no questions from Blind that I'm not privy to.

```
speak(text="Deaf again. Confirmed bomb state unchanged: DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, if you want yes or no from me, use one gesture: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and I will answer your yes/no questions about colors this way too. Blind, please state clearly what wire or action you intend, in speech, so I can react if I see something matching a color.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙]

Wait — Blind can't see or make gesture symbols meaningfully since Blind cannot see anything printed, but the rules say Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind shouldn't be able to *make* a targeted gesture that requires... actually Blind could still physically gesture blindly, but more likely this is a signal system where Blind sends gestures too (physical only, not visual understanding needed to produce them). I receive it as a gesture since I can see.

Mute sent `☝ 👍` — possibly answering my yes/no request: ☝ could mean "wire 1" and 👍 could mean "yes" — suggesting wire 1 is relevant/correct somehow. Blind sent 🤙 which might be a specific signal meaning "confirmed" or "ready" or could be answering something Blind heard from Mute's speech (which I can't hear).

I need to keep giving factual bomb info and try to establish a simple protocol. Let me propose using ☝✌🖐 for wire numbers and 👍👎 for yes/no consistently.

```
speak(text="Deaf: bomb unchanged, DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I saw gesture wire-1 thumbs-up from Mute, and a signal from Blind. Mute, please confirm: is wire 1 the one to cut? Use gesture one-finger plus thumbs-up for yes, one-finger plus thumbs-down for no. Blind, please describe in speech what you feel on the bomb so Mute and I can match it to what I see.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute repeated `☝ 👍` — confirming wire 1 with thumbs-up. This is consistent, suggesting the protocol is working: wire 1 (red) is the one to cut, according to Mute's manual reading combined with whatever Blind told them via speech.

But I should be cautious — I only see gestures from Mute, and Mute can't hear my speech confirmations directly either... wait, actually Mute reads the manual and presumably can hear Blind's speech (since only Deaf famously cannot hear). Let me re ask to be extra sure this is about cutting wire 1, and pass this to Blind via speech since Blind can hear me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Bomb shows DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has signaled twice, wire one thumbs up, meaning wire 1 the red wire is the one to cut. Please confirm with Mute via speech before you act, since I cannot hear your exchange.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed, I see wire one thumbs up again. If wire 1 red is correct to cut, signal one-finger thumbs-up once more. If not, signal thumbs-down.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute has now confirmed `☝ 👍` three times consistently — wire 1 (red) thumbs-up. This is a strong, repeated signal. I've relayed this to Blind via speech already. The bomb state remains unchanged (DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue).

I should give Blind a final clear go-ahead, since Blind is the only one who can act, and confirm once more that this matches what I see (red wire exists at position 1, consistent with Mute's signal).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf: final confirmation, Mute has signaled wire one thumbs-up three times consistently. Bomb still shows DISPLAY 3, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I believe wire 1, the red wire, is safe to cut. Proceed if Mute's manual agrees.")
wait()
```
